edge_explainer: SELF-CORRECTION FIRST: an earlier pass of this court, working only from the press release and 10-Q, ruled that Aptiv was misdirecting - blaming a recovering China while the real damage sat in EMEA. The earnings-call transcript REFUTES that and I have reversed it. The CFO gave a quantified bridge attributing ~83% of the $300M sales cut to China (~$150M China domestic schedule weakness + ~$100M delayed China program ramps + ~$50M software timing). That is granular disclosure, not evasion. And decisively: Aptiv's geographic revenue is reported on a MANUFACTURING-LOCATION basis (10-Q Note 19), so European luxury OEMs building cars FOR EXPORT INTO CHINA book into the EMEA line - the EMEA collapse and the China story are ONE story seen from the factory side, not two competing explanations. Reading them as rival causes was a category error. WHAT CHINA ACTUALLY SHOWS: Q2-26 China revenue +5% against China production about -3% = +8pp growth-over-market. Aptiv is currently GAINING content share in China. H1 -4% implies Q1 about -12/-13%, so the realized trend is sharply improving; the cut is FORWARD H2 schedule risk (Clark: China retail sales down 20% YoY, local OEMs reducing H2 production). The bear framing of a melting global-OEM China book is mis-aimed on current evidence. WHERE SHARE HAS ALREADY MELTED - and it is the premium-multiple leg: against +10% Chinese production in 2025, H1-25 Asia Pacific Engineered Components grew +11.4% (at market) while Intelligent Systems/ASUX fell -11.8% (about -22pp UNDER market). The mechanism is documented, not theoretical: BYD is itself a top-3 ADAS supplier in China (Gasgoo Jan-May 2026: Bosch 10.4%, DENSO 9.4%, BYD 9.1%) and has closed the silicon loop with its 4nm 'Xuanji A3' (L3/L4, >2,100 TOPS) already in mass production across five wafer fabs; cockpit domain controllers are locally owned (Desay SV 15.2%, Huawei 7.1%, ECARX 6.3%); Aptiv appears on none of these leader boards and its own 10-K competition section names ZERO Chinese companies. BUT BOUND IT: Intelligent Systems Asia Pacific is $278M/quarter = 8.5% of total revenue, while Engineered Components carries ~70% of Aptiv's Asia-Pacific dollars ($602M vs $278M) with no insourcing evidence in either direction. The documented kill-channel hits Aptiv's SMALLEST China pocket - which caps the structural bear case and is why this lowers the multiple rather than triggering an exit. CORE FINDING (unchanged and reinforced): the segment justifying the premium multiple is the broken one. Intelligent Systems (the renamed Advanced Safety & User Experience - the seed had the RemainCo segment names wrong) is 46% of revenue but grew -0.4% in Q2 with H1 adjusted EBITDA DOWN 3.1% and GAAP operating income down 13.8%; 91% of consolidated Q2 EBITDA growth came from Engineered Components. Inside it, 'Sensors and Compute' ($2.67B H1 = 42% of the whole company) is SHRINKING -0.9%, while the genuinely growing 'Software and Services' line is $297M H1 = 4.7% of revenue. The release is headlined 'Strong Operating Performance and Significant Progress Diversifying Towards Non-Auto Markets' and the CEO leads with 'reacceleration in revenue growth,' Robotics and a Drone win - all true, but the marketed takeaway (a re-accelerating technology company) diverges from its own segment data. Fully disclosed in the same morning's 10-Q: emphasis-management, REVIEW-FLAG not exclude, consequence is valuation. Independent price-channel corroboration: VGNT, Aptiv's own commodity wiring-harness castoff, rose +9.4% the day the parent fell 16% and trades at a HIGHER EV/EBITDA (6.66x) than the parent. STRONGEST HONESTY FINDING - systematic de-quantification since FY2022, four confirmed absences: (1) stopped naming customers after FY2022 (the last table named GM 9%, Stellantis 9%, Ford 8%, VW 8%, Tesla 5%, Geely 5%, SAIC-GM 3%); (2) stopped printing an above-market-growth number after FY2022 (FY20/21/22 printed 10%/15%/11%; three 10-Ks since contain none); (3) gave no growth-over-market figure on the Q2-26 call in the quarter where it was the central question; (4) names no Chinese competitor anywhere. The one China statistic volunteered - '>75% of new business awards in China with local OEM customers' (FY2025 10-K) - is BOOKINGS not revenue, appeared exactly once with no prior-year comparable, and Clark disclaimed its read-through on the call ('our revenues don't match the bookings mix over the last two years'). Nothing said today is false; but the burden of proof has been quietly shifted onto the analyst, who cannot discharge it from primary sources. That alone justifies a lower multiple. GROWTH-OVER-MARKET, stated honestly: Q2-26 +3pp, H1-26 +2pp (verbatim from the MD&A: volumes +3% vs flat production/flat AWM; H1 volumes +1% vs -1% production/-1% AWM). Full-year cross-check: $12,700M guide vs a DERIVED FY25 New-Aptiv base of ~$12,354M = +2.8% reported / +2% adjusted (management's own characterisation) against a market of -1% to -2% = +3 to +4pp. Both methods agree. IMPORTANT: the seed's '+6-8pp historic' benchmark is NOT verifiable from primary sources and is not relied on - the correct statement is 'GoM is now +2 to +4pp and the company stopped publishing the metric in FY2022.' Peer-filed 2026 production assumptions corroborate a China-specific (not global) weakness: Autoliv global LVP about -2.5%; Magna cut China 0.8M units while RAISING NA and Europe; Gestamp H1-26 actuals China -5.3%. WHY IT IS STILL NOT AN ENTRY: the Q2 beat is genuine and honestly constructed (I tested it - the $44M debt-extinguishment gain sits in Other income but is explicitly REMOVED in the Adjusted Net Income recon; residual other income $14M vs $15M LY; the beat is ~$0.13 operating margin plus ~$0.06 from a 15.1% adjusted tax rate vs ~18% guided). Balance sheet safe, cap structure clean (zero converts, zero preferred, zero warrants; NCI and redeemable NCI both to $0 in H1). Top-10 customer concentration fell 56% -> 44% post-spin. This is the FIRST cut of the year (Feb guide = May guide, identical line by line) and small (-3.4% EPS). AGAINST: the cut deleted the TOP of every range rather than resetting the base (high end fell 2.0x-5.0x more than the low end; FCF high -$125M vs low -$25M) - a confidence withdrawal; GAAP guidance went UP (+2.7% EPS) on below-the-line items while the adjusted operating measure fell; and FCF was cut only 10% after H1 came in at -$196M vs +$264M LY, a $460M YoY deterioration, leaving H2 to deliver +$871M and CFO of $1,238M against H1's $82M. Steelmanned: Aptiv's shape IS back-loaded (FY25 total-company FCF $1,529M with $651M in Q4 alone); allocating New Aptiv's ~74% pro forma share puts estimated H2-25 FCF at ~$870M, so the H2-26 ask is roughly FLAT YoY. The guide does not require a heroic H2 - it requires a NORMAL H2 after an abnormal H1 with zero degradation. Coin-flip, not fraud. DE-RATE vs DERAILMENT: early DERAILMENT - estimates fell today and the multiple followed; the HUBS/CTSH/SAP compressed-multiple-on-stable-estimates winner pattern is absent. PATH: today IS the 52-week low, 0 days since, on 6.8x ADV - not a late bounce, but the most dangerous point on the drift curve. Prior tape: -7.9% on the 2026-05-05 in-line Q1 with a REAFFIRMED guide (market discounted the reaffirmation because standalone Q1 EBITDA margin was 16.3% vs an 18.6% FY guide), then -16.6% today - two consecutive earnings breaks. Also REFUTED: the seed's '-46% off 52w high' - the post-spin high is $78.49 (2026-06-03), so -39.2%; -46% only works against the pre-spin company that still owned EDS. VALUATION: at $47.72, 6.20x EV/EBITDA, 8.37x P/E, 6.8% FCF yield on the CUT guide - but the verified live peer set puts APTV in the UPPER HALF (ALV 6.75x, VGNT 6.66x, BWA 6.54x, MGA 5.37x, VC 5.35x, LEA 4.60x). 'Cheap vs peers' is REFUTED. 'Cheap vs own franchise value' is UNTESTABLE this session - Aptiv's own historical multiple band is UNVERIFIABLE for three confirmed reasons (pre-spin IBKR bars carry an unrecoverable corporate-action adjustment; the pre-2026 denominator is a different company that owned EDS; IBKR daily history starts 2021-08-09). Mid-court correction recorded: my first pass used a 6.75x base for +17.6% edge; the peer band showed that assumed a re-rate to the TOP of the comp set, so I re-based to 6.5x and the edge fell to +11.3% - my prior was too GENEROUS, the opposite of my usual conservative-FV failure mode. Sensitivity IS the ruling: base 5.5x -> -0.2% edge, 7.5x -> +24.2%. A +/-1x assumption is worth +/-$12/share, larger than the entire computed edge. Market-implied decomposition at $47.72: p_bear about 0.56-0.61 vs my 0.35 - I am ~20pp less bearish than the tape, on scenarios I cannot pin better than +/-$12. DISCOVERY_STATE = CROWDED: ~$9.9B cap, 20+ analysts, $160M/day 90-day dollar volume - zero informational asymmetry. Across four news sweeps ZERO commentators mention Intelligent Systems (coverage uniformly blames China), and only ONE price target moved all day (Baird 68->59) against a standing deck of JPM 75 / Wells 77 / Goldman 74 / UBS 80 / TD Cowen 93 struck at $57-77 tape. The sell-side has not repriced; a downgrade wave is a live near-term negative and a reason to sit BELOW the market. RESPONSE TAXONOMY: dominant finding is valuation -> price gate; secondary is business-risk -> size cut; both applied, hence a sub-cap below-market ladder rather than an entry. NOT AI-complex (auto/industrial cyclical; Robotics/Drone references attach to a $297M-H1 software line = 4.7% of revenue) - entry does not require the AI cycle holding, no conflict with the frozen AI-BREAK|2027-12-31 @ 0.45 house call. No portfolio conflict: no APTV, no VGNT, no auto-supplier exposure (positions polled 2026-08-04). Respects the prior VGNT 3/10 PASS from this same queue. SCORE HELD AT 5 after the China evidence landed - the corrections roughly offset. China is LESS structurally threatening than the seed assumed (+8pp GoM, insourcing confined to 8.5% of revenue, cut candidly bridged); the honesty picture is WORSE than the filings alone suggested (four-instance de-quantification since FY2022). What did not move is the binding constraint: APTV is not cheap against a verified peer set and the edge is smaller than the multiple error bar. No China finding could have lifted this past a 5. TOP UNVERIFIABLE #1: the 'Other, net -$331M' working-capital line in H1 operating cash flow - the largest unexplained drain, not decomposed anywhere in the 10-Q, the swing factor in the entire FY FCF guide, and the difference between 'Q4 timing reversal' and 'permanent post-spin cash-cycle rebasing.' Every scenario probability is sensitive to it. TOP UNVERIFIABLE #2 (new, and load-bearing): connector/Engineered-Components insourcing by BYD/Geely - no evidence found in either direction, and this matters MORE than the ADAS insourcing that is documented, because EC carries ~70% of Aptiv's Asia-Pacific dollars while the documented ADAS channel hits only 8.5% of revenue. Also unverifiable: exact China % of revenue (never disclosed; upper bound 26.4% Asia Pacific on a manufacturing-location basis, which overstates it); any '% of China revenue from local OEMs' statistic (does not exist in any primary source); Aptiv's own historical multiple band; H2-25 New Aptiv FCF (~$870M, derived, and the entire FCF steelman rests on it); street Q3 consensus.

china_channel_resolution.question: court Q1 - is APTV winning Chinese-OEM content or is the book legacy-JV concentrated (the melting side)?
china_channel_resolution.answer: NEITHER cleanly, and the decomposition the question asks for DOES NOT EXIST in any primary source. Aptiv has never published a split of China revenue between global-OEM JVs and Chinese domestic OEMs, and names no BYD/Geely/Chery/Xiaomi program win in any filing. What IS establishable: (a) Aptiv is currently OUTGROWING the Chinese market by ~8pp (Q2-26 China +5% vs about -3% production); (b) the share loss that already happened was in 2025 and lived ENTIRELY in Intelligent Systems (H1-25 APAC -11.8% vs +10% China production, about -22pp under market) while Engineered Components grew +11.4% at market; (c) the insourcing mechanism is documented (BYD 9.1% ADAS share, own 4nm silicon, five wafer fabs; Desay SV/Huawei/ECARX own cockpit controllers; Aptiv on no leader board); (d) but Intelligent Systems Asia Pacific is only 8.5% of total revenue, whereas Engineered Components carries ~70% of Aptiv's Asia-Pacific dollars and shows no insourcing evidence either way.
china_channel_resolution.long_run_insourcing_exposure_pct_of_reve: ~8.5% documented (Intelligent Systems Asia Pacific); ~18% of revenue is Engineered Components Asia Pacific where the threat is UNQUANTIFIED in either direction; the harness business most exposed to Chinese vertical integration left with Versigent on 2026-04-01
china_channel_resolution.only_chinese_oem_named_on_the_call: BYD - and it was cited as a DELAYED export-vehicle program inside the guidance-cut explanation, not as a win
